subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable TUI plain-text accessibility config mode, and what public key/default/replacement semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but repository policy treats new config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive product decisions that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Add TUI plain-text mode
options.body: Add a documented plain-text accessibility mode across config, generated surfaces, TUI startup, tool display, selectors, and tests while preserving rich glyph output by default.

options.title: Fold into broader accessibility design
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers define a larger accessibility surface covering TUI glyph output plus related screen-reader workflows.

options.title: Decline the config knob
options.body: Close as not planned and document that current TUI output remains glyph-rich by design, accepting the accessibility tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Add TUI plain-text mode
recommendation.body: Add a documented plain-text accessibility mode across config, generated surfaces, TUI startup, tool display, selectors, and tests while preserving rich glyph output by default.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across the TUI, tool-display metadata, and config schema surfaces implicated by this decision.
